title: Tor-independent base change for a perfect tensor factor
statement: Let f:X\to S be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme], let g:S'\to S be a morphism with S=\operatorname{Spec}(R) and S'=\operatorname{Spec}(R'), and form X'=X\times_S S' with projection g_X:X'\to X and f':X'\to S' [def-pc-fibre-product]. Assume f and g are Tor independent: for every x\in X and s'\in S' over the same s\in S, \operatorname{Tor}_i^{\mathcal O_{S,s}}(\mathcal O_{X,x},\mathcal O_{S',s'})=0 for i>0. If P is a perfect complex on X [def-pc-perfect-complex] and K\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(X) [def-pc-derived-category], then the canonical base-change morphism $$Lg^*Rf_*(P\mathbin{\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_X}}K)\longrightarrow Rf'_*\bigl(Lg_X^*P\mathbin{\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_{X'}}}Lg_X^*K\bigr)$$ [def-pc-derived-pullback, def-pc-derived-direct-image, def-weil-derived-tensor] is an isomorphism in D(\mathcal O_{S'}).

source.place: Tag 0AVW, lemma-affine-morphism-and-hom-out-of-perfect (proof of case (1), after tensor-Hom identification)

proof.text: Apply the stalk comparison [lem-pc-tor-independent-perfect-pullback-comparison] to P. The Tor-independence hypothesis gives, at every x' over x, the required stalkwise isomorphism for the canonical identity map Lg_X^*P\to Lg_X^*P, so this map satisfies the stalkwise base-change condition of the single-complex criterion.

source.place: Tag 0AVW, lemma-compare-base-change proof: local affine reduction and Tor-independent comparison of derived tensors

proof.text: Use tensor inheritance [lem-pc-rf-single-complex-inherited-tensor-condition] with K=P, K'=Lg_X^*P and the identity map Lg_X^*P\to Lg_X^*P, and E=K (the given quasi-coherent derived object). It gives the stalkwise condition for the induced map Lg_X^*(K\otimes^L P)\to Lg_X^*K\otimes^L Lg_X^*P.

source.place: Tag 0DJA, part (1), tensor inheritance of the single-complex base-change condition

proof.text: Apply the qcqs single-complex base-change theorem [lem-pc-rf-single-complex-qcqs-induction] to the map from Step 2. Its objects lie in the quasi-coherent derived categories, as that theorem requires: P is perfect, hence has quasi-coherent cohomology (Stacks Tag 08DB), so P and K\otimes^L P lie in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(X), and Lg_X^*P and Lg_X^*K\otimes^L Lg_X^*P lie in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(X') [lem-pc-derived-pullback-tensor-qcoh]. Since f is quasi-compact and quasi-separated, it yields an isomorphism Lg^*Rf_*(K\otimes^L P)\to Rf'_*\bigl(Lg_X^*K\otimes^L Lg_X^*P\bigr).

The derived-pullback tensor-product comparison [lem-pc-derived-pullback-tensor-product] identifies Lg_X^*(K\otimes^L P) with Lg_X^*K\otimes^L Lg_X^*P. Transporting the isomorphism of Step 3 across this canonical identification and the symmetry of derived tensor gives exactly the displayed base-change morphism.
